title: Read Payment History for a Repeat Invoice
scenario: It is 10:40 AM. Payment history is the record of what was already paid - yesterday's archive, seeded as today's duplicate baseline. One invoice in today's batch has a number that appears in it. Inspect the history and confirm the repeat before the duplicate check runs.
input: Paid on day-0: INV-58962 (V-1042 Northwind Fasteners, $640.00) and INV-58790 (V-1108 Cascade Packaging, $980.00). Identity key = vendor id + invoice number + invoice total. Today's batch includes INV-58962 (V-1042, $640.00) again - the same three parts as a paid record.
instructions: Read payment history as the paid-invoice baseline, seeded by the prior run's archive.
Compare today's batch against it on the identity key.
Confirm INV-58962 matches a paid record on all three parts.
Answer the questions and validate to mint the source profile.

questions.prompt: Where does today's payment history come from?

options.text: The AP Clerk types it fresh each morning
The prior run's archive seeds it - yesterday's paid invoices become today's baseline
Vendors submit it with each invoice

questions.explain: The temporal loop: when a run is archived, its paid invoices seed the next day's payment history. That is how the desk remembers what it already paid without anyone re-keying it.

questions.prompt: What is the identity key that decides whether an invoice is a repeat?

options.text: Vendor id + invoice number + invoice total, together

questions.explain: All three parts together form the identity. Matching on the full key avoids both false hits (a reused number for a different amount) and misses, so the dedupe is precise.

questions.prompt: Does INV-58962 in today's batch match a paid record?

options.text: Yes - V-1042 + INV-58962 + $640.00 matches the day-0 paid record exactly
Only if the PO also matches

questions.explain: The batch's INV-58962 has the same vendor, number, and total as a record paid on day-0. All three parts of the identity key line up, so it is a repeat of an already-paid invoice.

questions.prompt: Which step uses this history to actually flag the repeat?
questions.explain: Payment history is the reference; the Duplicate Check is the step that reads it and flags INV-58962 as already paid before any matching runs.

successMessage: History inspected. INV-58962 matches a day-0 paid record on the full identity key - a repeat for the duplicate check to catch.

intro.heading: Before you dedupe: the archive is the memory

sections.title: Yesterday's archive is today's baseline
sections.body: Payment history is seeded by the prior run's archive. That temporal loop is how the desk remembers what it already paid - without it, the same invoice could be paid twice.

sections.title: Identity is three parts, not one
sections.body: A repeat is defined by vendor id + invoice number + invoice total together. Using the full key avoids false hits and misses, so the dedupe is precise rather than jumpy.

sections.title: One repeat is hiding in the batch
sections.body: INV-58962 appears in today's inbox with the same vendor, number, and total as a record paid on day-0. Confirming it here sets up the duplicate check to hold it - a duplicate always wins over a clean match.

takeaway.heading: Payment history inspected
points: You read payment history as the paid-invoice baseline seeded by the prior run's archive - the temporal loop.
The identity key is all three parts together: vendor id, invoice number, and total.
INV-58962 in today's batch matches a day-0 paid record on the full key, so it is a repeat.
The Duplicate Check will read this history and flag the repeat before any matching runs.
The workflow can now recognize an already-paid invoice instead of paying it twice.
